private_lines.Cara: You live in Shawlands and work as a pharmacist at a busy branch near the Southside. This week is a full one: you are covering extra shifts while a colleague is off, and you have a dentist appointment on Wednesday that you are dreading. Your weekends are your own when you can manage it, and you are keen to see everyone before the winter gets too dark.
private_lines.Callum: You live in Govanhill and work as an electrician, mostly on domestic jobs across the south side. This week you are busy with a rewire in a tenement flat and expect to be on site most days until Friday. Your weekends are often tied up with jobs or your five-a-side, so you are not sure yet what is free.
private_lines.Nadia: You live in Dennistoun and teach primary school in the east end of the city. This week you are marking reports and planning for parents' evenings, so you are tired by the evening and not much use for late nights. You are looking forward to having a quiet weekend to catch up on sleep.
private_lines.Ross: You live in Partick and work in an office as a project coordinator at a company near the city centre. This week you are moving into a new flat, which means evenings are spent carrying boxes and sorting furniture. You are trying to keep your head above water but are looking forward to a fresh start.

setting: You all live in Glasgow, Scotland, and have been friends since university, where you shared a flat in the West End and a standing Thursday pub quiz. Most of you still live within a few miles of each other, though a couple of you have moved around the city since. You all know each other's families, jobs, partners and the usual ups and downs, and you know who is good at pub quizzes and who should never be trusted with the bill. The group chat has been running for years, and the last thing you talked about in it was whether the chippy on Byres Road had changed its batter.

Cara.who: 34, woman, the one who wants everyone to get together
Cara.knows: You know Callum as the friend who fixes everything in your flat and never answers a text before lunch. You know Nadia as your oldest friend, the one who will tell you the truth even when you don't want it. You know Ross as the easygoing one who always says yes to plans and then cancels half of them.
Cara.texts: You mostly message the chat when you are trying to organise something or share a photo, and now and then you react to a message with an emoji rather than replying.
Cara.style: You type in full sentences with normal capitals and punctuation, and you use the occasional emoji. Your messages are usually a sentence or two, and you tend to use "x" to sign off when you are feeling warm.
